pins.name: VBACKUP
pins.net: VDD_SNVS_IN (always-on 3.0 V) via 1 k, or GND via 10 k

circuit.role: event input unused: must not float, not to VBACKUP
no backup source: VBACKUP to ground
OR backup from the always-on rail [this design]
INT pull-up: existing wake-line pull-up to the 1.8 V SNVS rail (open drain)

supplies.VDD: 1.3-5.5 V timekeeping, 1.4-5.5 V interface (p7); EEPROM write needs >= 1.6 V
supplies.note: with CLKOUT disabled; a running 32.768 kHz output adds load-dependent current

logic: open-drain SDA and INT; input pins limited to VDD + 0.3 V (p127): pull-ups must not go to a rail above the chip's VDD, so VDD = +3V3 with the 3.3 V I2C_P bus
placement: Anywhere quiet; it is temperature-compensated. Keep the 100 nF at pin 6.
notes: Backup switch-over (EEPROM register C0h, BSM bits, p45): 00/11 off (as delivered), 01 direct switching (runs from whichever of VDD/VBACKUP is higher), 10 level switching (switches when VDD < 2.0 V and VBACKUP > 2.0 V). With VDD on +3V3 and VBACKUP on the always-on 3.0 V rail, level switching keeps time when the 3.3 V converter is off; in backup the I2C pins are disabled and INT still works but then needs its pull-up from VBACKUP's domain (p10, p58): the 1.8 V SNVS pull-up qualifies only if SNVS stays up.
If the 3.3 V rail is never switched off, use the no-backup circuit (VBACKUP to ground through 10 k).

CLKOUT: push-pull at VDD level, ON at delivery with 32.768 kHz; selectable 32.768 kHz, 1024, 64, 1 Hz or 8192 Hz-67 MHz in 8192 Hz steps (p62, p140). It can clock other chips, but the brain's 32 kHz input is not a 3.3 V pin: only through a divider/AC coupling, and the FC-135 crystal is already planned. Disable CLKOUT (NCLKE = 1, stored in EEPROM) if unused; if unused leave the pin floating, never tie it to a rail (p10).
INT is open drain, active low; alarm, timer, periodic update, temperature, event, voltage-low, switch-over and power-on interrupts (p10).
